beats.name: George Pake
beats.role: Xerox PARC. Told Business Week he didn't know how much paper he'd still want; not the 'paperless by 1990' claim usually attributed to him.

beats.text: The magazine predicted electronic record-handling by 1990.
beats.note: A separate claim from Pake's own hedge about a desk terminal by 1995; the two get merged in almost every retelling.

beats.text: US business paper use nearly doubled in three years.
beats.note: 850 billion pages in 1981 to 1.4 trillion by 1984, as photocopiers and early computers multiplied documents instead of replacing them.

beats.text: Office paper use rose again once email arrived.
beats.note: US office paper consumption grew more than 14% between 1995 and 2000.

beats.text: Paper use only started falling once everyone had a phone.

beats.line: Printing-writing paper capacity peaked around 2000; a quarter-century late.
